scope: Actual managed PostgreSQL integration against isolated disposable databases; not full application or live OAuth acceptance

cases.name: serializes concurrent exchanges into one immutable identity and account
never remaps an established subject or links a recycled email to a different subject
claims an invitation atomically and creates no account when the invitation is missing
terminates an accepted pg_sleep and permits a later query
shares the actual readiness query across callers and recovers on a fresh connection
aborts a timed-out transaction without committing its writes and recovers transactions
preserves model error mapping for unique constraints
quotes a custom schema for unqualified raw queries

previousAttempt.reason: All eight test cases passed, but cleanup failed because database comments require the shared-object catalog lookup.
previousAttempt.fix: Cleanup now checks shobj_description against its independent ownership marker before dropping a disposable database.

limitations: The identity integration cases inject an already verified provider identity; they do not complete live Google OAuth or validate a live provider token.
These tests use an operator administrator connection for disposable database administration and migrations; they do not establish runtime-role privileges.
Main application database migrations and runtime-role probes occur after this isolated test run and require separate evidence.
The Docker PostgreSQL 16 path remains available but was not executed on this workstation.
External messaging, application media authorization and published-site user journeys require separate acceptance checks.
